text: Let me remind you of the good news I gave you, which you received and still stand on.
It's saving you too, if you hold to what I told you — otherwise you believed for nothing.
The first thing I handed on to you, as it was handed to me: Christ died for our sins, as the Scriptures foretold,
he was buried, and he was raised on the third day, again as the Scriptures foretold,
and he appeared to Cephas, and then to the Twelve.
After that he appeared to over five hundred brothers and sisters at once, most of whom are still alive, though some have died.
Then he appeared to James, and then to all the apostles.
Last of all, as to one born at the wrong time, he appeared to me too.
I'm the least of the apostles, not even fit to be called one, because I persecuted God's church.
But by God's grace I am what I am, and that grace wasn't wasted — I've worked harder than any of them, though it was God's grace at work in me.
Whether it was me or them, this is what we preach, and this is what you believed.
But if we preach that Christ was raised, how can some of you say there's no resurrection of the dead?
If there's no resurrection, then Christ wasn't raised either.
And if Christ wasn't raised, our preaching is empty and so is your faith.
We'd even be caught lying about God, since we said he raised Christ — which he didn't, if the dead aren't raised.
If the dead aren't raised, Christ wasn't raised.
And if Christ wasn't raised, your faith is pointless and you're still in your sins.
Then those who died believing in Christ are lost.
If our hope in Christ is only for this life, we're the most pitiable people there are.
But in fact Christ has been raised, the firstfruits of those who have died.
Death came through one man, and the resurrection of the dead comes through one man.
As everyone dies in Adam, so everyone will be made alive in Christ.
Each in turn: Christ the firstfruits, then those who belong to him when he comes.
Then the end, when he hands the kingdom to God the Father after destroying every rule, authority and power.
He must reign until he's put all his enemies under his feet.
The last enemy to be destroyed is death.
For everything has been put under his feet — obviously not including God, who put it all under him.
When all is subject to the Son, the Son will himself be subject to God, so that God may be all in all.
Otherwise, what are people doing being baptized on behalf of the dead? If the dead aren't raised, why do it?
And why do we put ourselves in danger every hour?
I face death daily — I swear it by my pride in you.
If, humanly speaking, I fought wild beasts at Ephesus, what did I gain if the dead aren't raised? 'Let's eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.'
Don't be fooled: bad company ruins good habits.
Wake up and stop sinning — some of you don't know God. I say this to shame you.
Someone will ask, 'How are the dead raised? What kind of body will they have?'
Fool! What you sow doesn't come to life unless it dies first.
And what you sow isn't the body that will be, just a bare seed, of wheat or something else.
God gives it the body he chooses, each seed its own body.
Not all flesh is alike: humans, animals, birds and fish each have their own.
There are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies, each with its own splendor.
The sun has one glory, the moon another, the stars another, and star differs from star in glory.
So it is with the resurrection: sown perishable, raised imperishable;
sown in dishonor, raised in glory; sown in weakness, raised in power;
sown a natural body, raised a spiritual body. If there's a natural body, there's a spiritual one too.
So it's written: the first man Adam became a living being; the last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
The spiritual doesn't come first, but the natural, and then the spiritual.
The first man was from the earth, made of dust; the second man is from heaven.
Those made of dust are like the man of dust; those of heaven are like the man of heaven.
Just as we've borne the image of the man of dust, we'll bear the image of the man of heaven.
Here's what I'm saying: flesh and blood can't inherit God's kingdom, and the perishable can't inherit the imperishable.
Listen, I'm telling you a mystery: we won't all die, but we'll all be changed —
in a flash, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet. The trumpet will sound, the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.
This perishable body must put on the imperishable, and this mortal body must put on immortality.
When that happens, the saying will come true: 'Death has been swallowed up in victory.'
'Death, where is your victory? Death, where is your sting?'
The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ!
So, my dear brothers and sisters, stand firm. Let nothing move you. Give yourselves fully to the Lord's work, because you know your labor in the Lord isn't wasted.
